newsitem.title: USA: Bill introduced to make stable prices Fed priority.
newsitem.headline: Bill introduced to make stable prices Fed priority.

text.p: A key House Republican lawmaker said on Friday he had introduced new legislation to mandate price stability as the Federal Reserve's main goal.

"Price stability is important since it provides the essential foundation for sustainable long-run economic and employment growth," Jim Saxton, Chairman of the Joint Economic Committee of Congress, said in a statement.
The Humphrey-Hawkins act, which provides the framework in which the Fed operates, requires the central bank to seek balanced economic growth with maximum employment and price stability.
Saxton said some other countries, such as Australia, Canada and the United Kingdom, have successfully adopted price stability as the central bank's main goal.

"What the bill does is to clarify what the Fed has done, particularly over the past seven years - target inflation," Saxton told Reuters. "It seems to be a concept that works quite well internationally."
He warned, however, that it may take U.S. lawmakers some time to work through the bill.

"It's the kind of issue that members of congress have got to deal with over some period of time so they can understand it," he told Reuters. "It's going to take some time to work with the leadership to get to the point where everybody can focus on why this is a good idea."

Saxton added it was easy to adopt a policy of pursuing stable prices while inflation was at its current low levels. "The many benefits that have been achieved by lowering inflation...can be locked in with little cost," he said.
The bill requires the Fed to set numerical goals for price stability, to disclose any adjustment to the targets and to specify the timetable for achieving them.

Saxton said the measure would not alter or affect other policy goals "except to the extent that such goals conflict with, or are inconsistent with, price stability". ((--Knut Engelmann, Washington newsroom, 202 898-8377))
